macro.headline: Tech-led pullback, Energy and Financials leading rotation under the surface.
macro.story:
The tape is transitional. SPY closed at 743.29, down 1.0% on the day and 1.5% over five sessions, sitting right on its 50-day moving average but still 7.2% above its 200-day. QQQ is the weak link — down 4.2% over five days, below its 50-day, RSI 42, MACD histogram deeply negative at -2.81, and price tagging the lower Bollinger band. Breadth is balanced-to-mildly-constructive: 49% of S&P names bullish versus 25% bearish, 7 of 11 GICS sectors above their 50-day. VIX is 18.18 (up 5.9% over 5d) and the VIX3M/VIX ratio has compressed 11% in a week, meaning short-dated hedging demand is catching up to term structure. Gold is down 7.9% over 21d and silver -19.5%, while DXY is up 0.8% over the same window — a classic strong-dollar/weak-metals pairing.

The prevailing sentiment in the tracked conversation attributes the weakness squarely to semiconductors and mega-cap tech: the loudest bearish voices are pointing at chip ETFs and the tech complex specifically, while a smaller cohort continues to defend AI names like META, NBIS, and AAOI. The tracked chart reads flag two macro cross-currents worth naming — 30-year Treasury auctions clearing near 5.06% (highest since 2007), and foreign net purchases of US equities running near-record. There is also a supply-side wildcard being circulated: a Houthi 'maritime embargo' on Saudi shipping and Brent crude pushing above $90, though our own WTI print sits at 81.57 (up 4.4% in 5d, up 6.2% in 21d) — meaningful but not a shock. The dominant view frames this as 'classic rotation' out of high-beta tech into Health, Software (defensively), and Energy. That is consistent with our sector data: Energy is HOT with a score of 9.2, Financials HOT at 8.8, Real Estate HOT at 8.8, while Technology and the Nasdaq 100 sit at the bottom (score 1.8, RSI 42, below 50-day, MACD bearish).

The rotation is doing exactly what the Early-Runway signal was built to catch: Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing is halfway through a hot spell with top-decile RS and a rotation score of 0.97 — a validated tailwind. Diagnostics & Research, Staffing, Health Information Services, and REIT-Industrial are all still early in their runs (roughly 12–18% through a typical spell) with above-median to top-decile RS. Software-Application and Internet Content still print as Early-Runway on the industry ranking despite the sector-level tech weakness — a real tension the reader should hold: the rotation model likes select software pockets even as XLK bleeds.

Forward watch: is this a rotation (leaders rotate, index holds) or the start of a broader de-risking? Watch VIX through 20, QQQ's ability to reclaim its 50-day, DXY behavior around 101 (metals cannot bottom until DXY rolls), and whether the auctioned 30-year yield stabilizes below 5%. Positioning/sentiment context: not washed out, not euphoric — transitional. No validated market-timing signal is active; work bottom-up through the validated Early-Runway funnel.

Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.

Gold -7.9% on 21d, Silver -19.2%, and the entire GLD/SLV/GDX complex flipped to ACCELERATING_BEARISH — that is where money is leaving. XLV +7.2%, XLE +6.1%, XLF +4.5%, XLRE +4.1% is where it is arriving. SPY itself is only +1.1% on 21d; the index tape is quiet, but underneath the rotation is violent.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The regime prints CHOPPY (confidence 6/10, transitional), and cross-asset tape backs that up: SPY sits mid-Bollinger with RSI 51.8, VIX 18.1 in contango with VIX3M 20.5, breadth constructive but not thrusting (63.6% of sectors above 50SMA, 5d bullish/bearish 32/25). That is the mechanical explanation for the metals bleed and it is not a fade candidate. Yields are pressing higher across the curve (10Y 4.57, +2.35% on 21d, RSI 57); the backtest is explicit that the 10Y "ceiling" DOESN'T HOLD — treat rising yields as trend, not exhaustion. Same discipline applies to TLT at 84.29 (mean-reversion DOESN'T HOLD) and WTI at 81.55 (mean-reversion WEAK).

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Leadership is defensive-cyclical, not tech-cyclical. XLV, XLE, XLF, XLRE are the top four on 21d, all with vs50 positive. Industry rotation flow is into Consumer Electronics, Software - Infrastructure, and one unmapped bucket — nothing out, no flips, no new entrants in 14d, which says the rotation is additive rather than churning. XLC is only +1.8% and XLI +0.9% — the "AI adjacency" trade is not what is pulling the tape this week; it is health care and financials doing the lifting while semis digest a 258% run.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** Semiconductors are flagged CEILING — 13 months hot, +258% (a record-tying spell), and already -14.5% on 21d. That is manage-exits territory, not fresh entries; the trend is still up but the runway is spent. The in-range setups are earlier-innings: Software - Infrastructure is only 1 month into a hot spell with +3% gain vs +18% typical — early, with room. Internet Content & Information and Software - Application are in the same shape: 1 month hot, gains still negative-to-flat versus typical spells that run 6+ months. The cleanest un-run setup on the board is Banks - Regional with CFG coiling 96.4% on bullish flow, tucked inside a sector (XLF) that is already leading — that is where smart-money flow meets unextended price. Medical Care Facilities is the exception on the health side: 8 months hot and +43% is above-typical on both axes, so it is closer to mid-innings than early.
